chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 349: The Human Foundation — Bai Lingmiao’s Darkest Family Secret
chapter_meta_description: Bai Lingmiao discovers her ancestors built their shrine on layers of human sacrifice. As she buries the dead, she confronts a truth she can’t escape: she still can’t forgive Li Huowang for killing them.
og_title: The Foundation of Bones — Bai Lingmiao’s Reckoning in Dao Gui Yi Xian 349
og_description: A childhood memory leads Bai Lingmiao to a horrifying discovery beneath the Bai family shrine: hundreds of bodies, arranged like bricks, every hand painted with a lotus. Now she must bury them and ask herself if mercy can exist beside blood.
twitter_title: The Bai Shrine Was Built on Corpses — Chapter 349
twitter_description: Bai Lingmiao digs up more than she bargained for: a foundation of human sacrifice. She buries the dead, but she can’t bury the pain.

lore_anchors.definition: A ritual practice in ancient Chinese construction and mythology where living people or corpses were buried in foundations to appease earth spirits or empower a structure. In this novel, it is taken to a grotesque industrial scale.

A Buddhist symbol of purity and enlightenment, but in the context of the White Lotus Society, it also marks sect affiliation. Here, painted on the hands of sacrificed victims, it becomes a brand of ritual ownership.

A syncretic Chinese secret religious tradition, often millenarian and outlawed by imperial dynasties, centered on figures like the Unborn Venerable Mother (Wusheng Laomu). In the Dao-Twisted World, it is a hereditary cult with a bloody, hidden history.
The local mountain near Niuxin Village where Bai Lingmiao’s family shrine is located; the name means "Ox Heart Mountain."
The grizzled patriarch of the Lü opera troupe; a practical, sharp-tongued old man who has seen enough of life to offer grim wisdom, not comfort.
